articles.title: The Pitching Coach Mirage
articles.subtitle: A 3.7-run range across 33 pitching coaches looks like the most exploitable personnel signal in baseball. After a proper Bayesian shrinkage test, 32 of 33 effects collapse to noise.
articles.summary: Per-coach raw FIP delta on acquired pitchers spans Oscar Marin's −2.01 to Mel Stottlemyre Jr.'s +1.65 — a range that would be the most exploitable personnel signal in the trade market if it were real. Partial-pooling Bayesian shrinkage tests the claim honestly. One coach survives; thirty-two do not. The same model at the org level finds four credible signals — all in the direction of orgs that worsen acquired pitchers, none in the direction of orgs that fix them.

articles.title: The Edge Isn't in the Farm
articles.subtitle: Top GMs don't beat the market on prospect math — the decomposition isolates where the $5M gap actually comes from
articles.summary: Companion piece to The $5M GM Gap. Pearson correlations across 48 GMs reveal that prospect-side features (FV, MiLB grades, dev cluster) are essentially uncorrelated with per-trade dollar surplus, while big-league acquired player quality and organizational infrastructure (alumni networks, dev fit) carry the signal. Payroll is slightly negative — money is not the gap.

articles.title: The $5M GM Gap
articles.subtitle: Across 15 seasons and 4,327 trades, the average dollar surplus captured per deal varies by $5M depending on who runs the front office
articles.summary: Forty-eight GMs with 40+ trades since 2010 sort cleanly by per-trade dollar surplus, top to bottom. The top quartile captures $7.36M per deal; the bottom quartile captures $2.01M. The gap is statistically robust (ANOVA p=4.9×10⁻⁴, bootstrap CI on the gap [$4.05M, $6.69M]) and the names at the top of the leaderboard are not the names the prospect-evaluation press tends to celebrate.

articles.title: The International Pipeline Edge
articles.subtitle: Why some organizations consistently extract better ERA outcomes from acquired pitchers — and what the roster data says about why
articles.summary: Across FIP, xFIP, and SIERA — three independent ERA-family metrics — organizations with higher shares of international-born pitchers extract systematically better outcomes from acquired starters. The effect holds across 632 trade-pitcher observations from 2010–2024.

articles.title: Breadth Over Depth: The Award Pedigree Paradox
articles.subtitle: Getting several decorated players outperforms getting one star — and the data is unambiguous about it
articles.summary: A counterintuitive finding from Bayesian regression across 5,000+ trade legs: the share of acquired players with any award history predicts better outcomes, but the average award prestige per player predicts worse outcomes. Breadth is rewarded. Depth is penalized.

articles.title: The Strikeout Spike Signal
articles.subtitle: When a pitcher's K% is rising into a trade, both the strikeout rate and the ERA metrics deteriorate post-trade. The selling team knows something.
articles.summary: Pitchers with rising K% trajectories regress on both K% and ERA after a trade — the sell signal is complete. Pitchers with declining K% trajectories show the opposite pattern. A clean, symmetric finding across 142 acquisitions.
